university: Missouri University of Science and Technology

documents.unit: Teaching and Learning Center (GAI task force)
documents.title: Generative AI (GAI) Guidelines
documents.stance_why: The page offers faculty "three levels of GAI use" (green, yellow, red) and says instructors "have academic freedom to set acceptable levels", so it sets no single rule and hands the decision to instructors with a tier scheme; hence delegates with tiers.
documents.summary: A Teaching and Learning Center page presenting a Spring 2024 faculty task force's three-level (green/yellow/red) scheme for course GAI policies, with official icons for syllabi and assignments. It also cautions against AI checkers, lists teaching resources, and gives short student-facing advice to verify, cite and revise AI output.

units.why: The passage says a faculty task force produced guidelines to help instructors write "their own course policies", so the university leaves the rule to instructors; this is P04, informs-level (not P56, since it sets no principles).
units.anchor: guidelines that would assist S&T faculty with developing their own course policies

units.why: "three levels of GAI use in courses" defines named tiers, which is P05; it states the scheme, so modality is informs.
units.anchor: The task force produced three levels of GAI use in courses
units.frag_end: levels of GAI use in courses:

units.why: The page names a "red" level where "no use of GAI is acceptable"; it is one of the tiers (P05) and itself bans AI, so unit_stance is prohibit.
units.anchor: the red—no use of GAI is acceptable
units.frag_start: When an academic honesty issue is raised, a
units.frag_end: makes the case easier to address.
units.policy: The red level means no use of GAI is acceptable
units.fit_note: Only the red tier is described in text; green and yellow are defined only in images.

units.why: "recommends that faculty include their own written policy" is a recommendation (should) to instructors to state expectations in the syllabus, so P09 rather than P04.
units.anchor: the GAI task force recommends that faculty include their own written policy

units.why: The sentence argues wide use of the shared images "may promote more consistent student recognition of course GAI policies"; nearest type is P09 (communicating expectations) but it recommends a common visual, not a statement.
units.anchor: Widespread use of the above images by S&T faculty may promote more consistent student recognition
units.fit_note: Encourages faculty to use common official images so students recognize policies across courses; the type only covers stating expectations.

units.why: "automatically included in syllabi created using Simple Syllabus" is an institutional set-up that puts the levels in syllabi; closest is P09, though the university acts rather than instructors.
units.anchor: They will also be automatically included in syllabi created using Simple Syllabus
units.fit_note: The university inserts the images into syllabus material; it does not require instructors to write a statement.

units.why: "Instructors have academic freedom to set acceptable levels of GAI use" places the decision with each instructor, which is P04.
units.anchor: Instructors have academic freedom to set acceptable levels of GAI use

units.why: "students need to clearly understand the expectation from one instructor to another" gives the reason levels help: clear expectations across courses. P09 is nearest but this states a need, not a duty.
units.anchor: students need to clearly understand the expectation from one instructor to another
units.fit_note: States that students need clear expectations across instructors; no duty to write a statement.

units.why: "a clear statement on the syllabus such as the red ... makes the case easier to address" explains that a clear syllabus statement supports academic honesty cases. It does not classify misuse as misconduct (P36), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: a clear statement on the syllabus such as the red
units.frag_start: When an academic honesty issue is raised
units.frag_end: makes the case easier to address.
units.uncovered_note: A clear syllabus AI statement makes academic honesty cases easier to handle.

units.why: "tutoring, or the S&T Writing & Communication Center can help students operate within the rules" points students to human support, P72.
units.anchor: Student resources such as tutoring, or the S&T Writing & Communication Center can help students

units.why: A Harvard collection, a book, prompts and an article are offered as "useful examples of how GAI can be used in teaching" to help faculty learn about AI, P63.
units.anchor: Here are some useful examples of how GAI can be used in teaching

units.why: "The UM system does not endorse nor provide an AI checker" states the system position on detectors, fitting P39 (not relying on detectors).
units.anchor: The UM system does not endorse nor provide an AI checker
units.frag_end: shown to be highly unreliable and biased.

units.why: "Faculty are therefore cautioned against attempting to use this type of software" advises instructors not to use AI checkers because they are "highly unreliable and biased"; P39.
units.anchor: Faculty are therefore cautioned against attempting to use this type of software
units.frag_end: not been able to keep up.

units.why: "detection software has not been able to keep up" with updating GAIs is a factual reason detectors are unreliable; P39 informs.
units.anchor: detection software has not been able to keep up
units.frag_end: not been able to keep up.

units.why: "you must verify ... all claims and information" when GAI is allowed requires checking AI output, P31; the cite requirement is coded separately.
units.anchor: When GAI is allowed you must verify and cite all claims and information appropriately
units.policy: When GAI is allowed, students must verify all claims and information

units.why: The same sentence requires students to "cite all claims and information appropriately" when GAI is allowed, i.e. acknowledge sources of AI content, P24 (no tool or prompt details, so not P25).
units.anchor: you must verify and cite all claims and information appropriately
units.policy: When GAI is allowed, students must cite all claims and information appropriately
units.fit_note: Requires citing claims and information; does not state that AI use itself must be disclosed.

units.why: "GAI are known to hallucinate and may include bias" is a factual warning about unreliable output, the basis of P31.
units.anchor: GAI are known to hallucinate and may include bias

units.why: "Do not blindly trust the information an AI generates" directs students to evaluate output critically, P31.
units.anchor: Do not blindly trust the information an AI generates

units.why: Students "must also not adopt generated content without reflection and revision to make it your work": submitted work must become the student's own, P29 (P32 is about staying primary problem-solver, a weaker fit).
units.anchor: You must also not adopt generated content without reflection and revision

units.why: "recommended that each assignment ... be tagged as green, yellow, or red" recommends per-assignment tiers, P05, with should.
units.anchor: each assignment within the course or assignment be tagged as green, yellow, or red
units.frag_start: If an instructor designates different levels

units.why: "These icons can be used to tag individual assignments" says the official icons may be used per assignment, P05 with may.
units.anchor: These icons can be used to tag individual assignments

notes: Only one included document. The green/yellow/red level definitions are in images absent from the saved text, so only the red level could be quoted. The page is a TLC task-force guideline, not a binding policy.
